subject: Bridgewell demo recap — model recommendations, schema checks, and retry policy

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgewell demo recap — model recommendations, schema checks, and retry policy

Hi Sophie / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the deep context on how Bridgewell surfaces clinical summarization and triage decisions to care coordinators. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we saw today
- Source: clinical notes (short, semi-structured), average 400 tokens, 95th pct 1200 tokens
- Primary outputs: structured JSON summary (diagnosis codes + confidence), and an extractive list of follow-ups with timestamps
- Key concerns you raised: hallucination risk on sensitive fields, schema conformance for downstream systems, and predictable tail latency during morning peaks

Model candidates we recommend for initial evals- rw-inference/rw-7b-q4f: lower latency, good for fast iterate cycles- rw-inference/rw-13b-int8: better F1 on entity extraction while still cost-effective- meta/llama-3-70b-q8: higher raw quality for long-form disambiguation (use only for heavy-quality passes)

Attached: bridgewell_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt variations + expected JSON output), latency_benchmark_config.yaml (suggested load profile and target SLOs). I also dropped a short sample JSON schema (schema_example.json) in this thread for the structured output fields you'll need to validate.

Suggested next steps
1) Run the provided prompt set against rw-7b-q4 and rw-13b-int8 — sample benchmark script is in the Drive doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2cBridgewell-benchmark
2) Karthik / Marissa to pair with your engineering team on the schema/contract review (we recommend function-calling + strict schema validation at the service edge).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive to cover retries, idempotency, and KV-cache warmups (30–45m) — propose Tue/Thu next week; please share availability.

A couple of notes on quality regressions and observability- We'll include the prompt set and a small eval harness to record per-example metrics (ROUGE/F1/custom tolerances).- Redwood Optimize can suggest batching + quantization mixes and predict per-token cost impact — we'll include those estimates in the next delivery.

If Bridgewell wants, we can run a short, no-cost baseline (2k prompts) to show comparative quality and latency across the two models above — that usually surfaces the main tradeoffs quickly and helps procurement evaluate cost.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Subject: Re: Bridgewell demo recap — model recommendations, schema checks, and retry policy

Thanks, Evelyn —

This is great — the prompt set looks like a good starting point. A couple of quick clarifying questions from the engineering side: 
1) When you say "strict schema validation at the service edge," are you suggesting rejecting the response if it doesn't conform, or returning a best-effort result with a confidence flag? Our downstream systems expect stable keys and types and prefer rejection with a retry over silent best-effort.
2) For retries: what does Redwood recommend for idempotency tokens and duplicate suppression when the model function triggers external actions (e.g., flagging a patient record)? We need a pattern that avoids double-actions if a late token arrives.

Also, hallucinations are our biggest worry. Can you include an example of the kinds of failure modes you saw when running the prompt set? A small set of failing examples will help us write the regression tests.

Sophie Turner
Head of Engineering, Bridgewell AI
sophie.turner@bridgewell.ai

Subject: Re: Bridgewell demo recap — model recommendations, schema checks, and retry policy

Hi Sophie —

Good questions — quick answers and an implementation sketch from the infra side: 

1) Schema enforcement pattern- We recommend function-calling with an explicit JSON schema for the structured output. In practice we do the following:  a) call model with function schema and parse the result b) run a lightweight validator (AJV-style) client-side c) if validation fails, return HTTP 409 (schema_mismatch) to the caller with the model payload attached for audit. Bridgewell's choice: reject-and-retry (recommended) or accept-with-flag. Given your downstream need for stable keys, reject-and-retry is the safer default.

2) Retry & idempotency pattern for external actions- Use a generated idempotency token per user-intent (e.g., intent_id derived from patient+visit+prompt-hash). Include that token in the call metadata and persist action-state server-side. If a retry arrives with the same token, respond with the recorded action result. For asynchronous external actions, return a 202 with an operation id and let the client poll. We can provide a small reference implementation as part of the deep-dive.

3) Handling hallucinations and regression tests- We ran the prompt set across rw-7b-q4 and rw-13b-int8 and captured a small set of failure modes (attached as a comment block in the Drive doc). Typical patterns: entity hallucination when context truncation occurs, and occasional numeric mis-attribution in long chains. Mitigations: stricter context-window management, aggressive prefix caching for known fields, and a lightweight determinism check for critical fields.

4) Operational suggestions from Redwood Optimize- For Bridgewell’s traffic profile (spikes in mornings), start with rw-13b-int8 for mid-quality passes with 8–16 token batching and reserve a small pool of rw-7b-q4 for low-latency prompts. We’ll propose an autoscale policy that keeps tail latency under 350ms for 95th pct.

Next steps
- Evelyn / Karthik: propose Tue 05/14 or Thu 05/16 for the technical deep-dive.
- Bridgewell: confirm preferred policy (reject-and-retry vs accept-with-flag) so we can bake it into the sample code.

Attaching a small schema example (schema_example.json) and linking the benchmark doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2cBridgewell-benchmark

—Marissa
